Dura Supreme Cabinetry celebrates 34th Kids Switch Day
November 25, 2026 | 10:01 am CST
Dura Supreme Cabinetry celebrates 34th Kids Switch Day
For the past 34 years, every employee that has a 5th grader in their life, be it a parent or grandparent, is invited to bring them to Dura's annual Kids Switch Day event. Photos by Dura Supreme.

HOWARD LAKE, Minn. — What started out as a Cub Scout project in the early 1990s is now a highly anticipated event every November at Dura Supreme Cabinetry. For the past 34 years, every employee that has a 5th grader in their life, be it a parent or grandparent, is invited to bring them to Dura's annual Kids Switch Day event.

Kids Switch students typically step away from this event with a newfound sense of honor for what their parent or grandparent does for work; an understanding of what it means to work hard, take care in the quality of their work, and get a feel for the manufacturing and woodworking industry. It can also inspire them to start building good habits at school that will help them be successful in their future careers.
This year, Rory, who works in Finishing Lab and is a sprayer trainer, presented the traditional inspirational speech. This part of the class teaches how important it is to be a good student and how those same traits carry over to being a good employee one day.
Other topics were discussed like “What is manufacturing?” and how important quality, safety, and innovation are to the industry.

Throughout the class, students are encouraged to break into discussions with the group and share ideas on how their efforts at school or home can help build positive habits so they can work towards success in their future careers.

Factory tour
Volunteer tour guides – Gary, Pat, and Tony – took the children on a walk throughout the facility, teaching them how a cabinet is made from start to finish as they visit each workstation.
During the tour, every child gets to make a special stop to see their parent or grandparent and hear them explain and demonstrate what their role is at Dura Supreme to the tour group.
Dura notes that this experience is special, in getting to see first-hand what a workday looks like in cabinet manufacturing facility.

The Build-A-Cabinet Project
After the tour, the class meets in the lunchroom for our Build-A-Cabinet project! Environmental Health and Safety Manager, Tom, gives a presentation on safety and demonstrate the how to properly and responsibly use the tools they will need to make their cabinet. Tom has over 30 years of experience at Dura Supreme and has been one of our coaches for Kids Switch Students over the years. Once they understand how to use the tools everyone dives into this fun hands-on activity.

"Over the past 15 years that I’ve been at Dura Supreme Cabinetry, Kids Switch Day is a truly inspiring event for everyone involved every year," notes Mandi Juskiewicz, marketing manager. "I love seeing the faces of my co-workers throughout our facility, filled with smiles for the children. You can feel the strong presence of pride for what we do radiating through the building. You can see the children throughout the day understanding and gaining their own pride in what their parent or grandparent does for a living.

It is a blessing to work for a company that not only supports their employees in many ways but makes the investment to support our children/grandchildren and their future careers. We hope all the students this year walked away inspired! We can’t wait for next years class!"
To see the full details of the day, visit durasupreme.com/blog.
